subject: Activation: BrightLayer inference integration — cost & perf plan
body:
From: Amy Leung <amy.leung@brightlayer.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Activation: BrightLayer inference integration — cost & perf questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited to move forward. Before we kick off the activation sprint, procurement and engineering asked for a concise plan that covers the cost/performance tuning steps we'll take during onboarding. Specifically:

- Target P95 latency SLOs for chat and batch workloads
- Typical batching and cache policies you'd implement for our traffic profile (short prompts, many concurrent users)
- Recommended quantization profiles and expected token-cost savings
- Routing/fallback policy if peak traffic exceeds the reserved quota

I've attached a small sample of our production prompts and a short list of procurement items we'll need (PO timeline, SOC2). Can you share a proposed sprint plan and which Redwood folks will own the tuning tasks?

Also cc'ing procurement at procurement@brightlayer.ai for visibility.

Thanks,
Amy Leung
VP Product, BrightLayer
amy.leung@brightlayer.ai
Attachment: brightlayer_sample_prompts.json (attachment stub, 12 KB)
Attachment: SOC2_Summary.pdf (attachment stub, 220 KB)

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Amy Leung <amy.leung@brightlayer.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Activation: BrightLayer inference integration — cost & perf questions

Hi Amy — great to hear and thanks for the attachments. Monica (CS lead) will own the activation sprint and Karthik (solutions) will own quantization and routing recommendations. Below is a compact 3-week activation sprint draft focused on cost/perf outcomes; happy to adapt based on your calendar.

Week 0 (prep, concurrent):
- Collect traffic traces & sample prompts (we already have the file you attached).
- Grant read-only access to a shared Drive folder (Drive link sent separately).
- Kickoff meeting to align SLOs and success criteria.

Week 1 (baseline + profiling):
- Run baseline load with current prompts; capture cold/warm latencies, token counts, and model selection mix.
- Identify top 10 prompt families for KV-cache and prefix caching.
- Deliver: Baseline metrics + recommended batching targets.

Week 2 (iterative tuning):
- Apply batching policy (auto-adaptive batch target + per-route override).
- Enable prefix/KV cache TTL experiments; measure hit rate and P95 improvement.
- Test recommended quantization profiles on a mirror workload (safety offload to lower-capacity nodes).

Week 3 (rollout & verification):
- Canary routing with 10/30/100% steps and rollback criteria.
- Final cost-projection and handoff doc (runbook + config snippets).

Attachments: quant-profiles.csv (profiles we plan to test), cost-projection-sheet.xlsx (estimate stub).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) 30-minute kickoff Friday (Aug 25) 10:00 AM PT or Monday (Aug 28) 9:00 AM PT — which works?
2) Share any additional sample traces (top endpoints + 1% anonymized logs).

I'll be the mailbox owner for the engagement; Monica will run the day-to-day tuning sprints.

Best,
Priyom Das
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Leung <amy.leung@brightlayer.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Aug 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Activation: BrightLayer inference integration — cost & perf questions

Amy / team — looping in the concrete checklist we'll execute during the sprint. I'm posting the tuning items in chronological order (oldest -> newest).

1) Baseline collection (24–48h):
- Capture representative 95/99 percentiles at cold/warm starts per route.
- Extract median prompt length, token distribution, and most frequent system prompts.
- Deliverable: baseline-report.pdf (summary metrics).

2) Batching strategy:
- Default: adaptive batching with target token latency budget = 200ms for chat short-turns; allow route-level override for heavy routes.
- Safety: enforce per-request max_latency_ms and per-batch max_tokens to prevent tail amplification.
- Goal: reduce per-token cost by 20–35% on high-concurrency endpoints.

3) Caching & prefetch:
- KV cache reuse where session affinity exists; prefix caching for templates with high reuse.
- TTL suggestions: 5–15 minutes for interactive sessions; longer for stable response templates.
- Instrument hit-rate dashboards (we'll add traces to your console view).

4) Quantization plan:
- Start with a conservatively aggressive 4-bit QK-packed profile (Q4_compat) for throughput-sensitive routes; compare against Q8_eco for quality-sensitive ones.
- Smoke test offline with 5000 sample requests (we'll run side-by-side A/B).
- Expected delta: ~25–40% token-cost reduction for chat workloads with minimal quality degradation in short-turn prompts.

5) Routing & fallbacks:
- Primary: region-local low-latency pool (reserved capacity).
- Secondary: burst pool (lower-cost instances / different quant profile) with automatic fallback if reserved pool latency > target.
- Canary policy: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with automated regressions on scorecards (latency, top-k accuracy for a prompt set).

6) Rollout verification and runbook:
- Define rollback triggers: +20% P95 or >3% quality regressions in evaluation set.
- Produce the final runbook with exact config blocks you can paste into the Redwood console.

Attachments referenced: quant-profiles.csv (profiles and sample metrics). Please also share a prioritized prompt set (top 50) so we can fast-track the A/B test.

I will lead the tuning sessions and be the point for runbook delivery.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

We'll prep the prioritized prompt set and share a 1% anonymized trace for the baseline. Meeting Friday 10:00 AM PT works for us.

—Amy

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Activation: BrightLayer inference integration — cost & perf questions

Hi Amy — quick answers to the three bullets from procurement/ops: 

1) SOC2: We can provide a downloadable redacted SOC2 report for procurement teams; for customers with enterprise contracts we can also arrange a secure read-only link under NDA (common for Private deployments).

2) Quantization behavior: Quantization (Q4_compat vs Q8_eco) will introduce small distributional changes on low-confidence tokens — not bit-for-bit identical. In our validation runs we flag regressions using a prompt holdout set and guard canary percentages accordingly. We recommend starting at 10% canary and running 48–72h checks against both latency and our automated quality metrics.

3) Billing: Redwood supports both direct PO invoicing and AWS Marketplace procurement for customers in the Marketplace. For Marketplace deals there is a short onboarding step; procurement@brightlayer.ai can share preferred billing flow and I'll loop in our finance partner if needed.

Estimated impact callout: with the recommended batching and Q4 profile we expect a 25–35% reduction in per-token expense for your chat route under simulated traffic (detailed numbers in cost-projection-sheet.xlsx).

Next: we'll confirm the Friday kickoff invite; Monica and I will bring the profiling scripts and quant benchmark harness.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
